issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-5a0dc962 (umbrella). Depends on the regression-test child.

Run scripts/build-from-archive.sh for the pinned commit recorded in pinned-binaries/COMMITS.md and compare the resulting binary's sha256 against the value recorded with that pin (BUILD_PROCEDURE.md currently records 6561869ba87fa1391967abf6877e51ef6425301b -> 0690918612738e0ff4717e9a9d54434a6bc734b67890fe99d767c5de780d02be).

Acceptance:
- The run completes with the shared checkout untouched (the regression-test child stays green)
- The comparison result is recorded in this bead's closing note
- If the sha256 does not reproduce, document the root cause (toolchain, feature flags, or profile drift) in the closing note and either correct the recorded metadata to the reproducible value or file the follow-up — never claim success without a match or a documented explanation
issue.notes:
COMPARISON RESULT (2026-09-03, worker claude-code-glm-4.7-glm-tunnel): NO MATCH — and the comparison as specified cannot run, for three independent, verified reasons.

(1) PINS ARE UNREACHABLE OBJECTS. git archive fails with 'fatal: not a tree object' for every recorded pin: af023ad, 946a727, 1ee45e3, e115609, f25ab5c (COMMITS.md) and 6561869 (BUILD_PROCEDURE.md). The repo is not shallow; origin/main (63c2ee8) is present locally and does not contain them; no other remote ref (recovery branch is unrelated f012/f013 work) holds them. These SHAs are the force-pushed-away lineage; content twins on the restored lineage (merge b057d27) carry the same messages under different SHAs: ea4e317 = release-0.2.4 message, c8836e0 = reproducible-build-docs, 861cdcb = binary-variant test suite, b0d7840 = attempts-binary docs. scripts/build-from-archive.sh does not exist yet (beadrs-53e55a45 / beadrs-41eb03d3), so no archive build could be attempted even against a twin.

(2) THE BUILD_PROCEDURE.md PAIR IS DOUBLY ORPHANED. 6561869 is unreachable AND sha256 0690918612738e0ff4717e9a9d54434a6bc734b67890fe99d767c5de780d02be matches NO committed artifact in pinned-binaries/ — that binary was never committed. By contrast all four committed pin binaries (bead-pre-feature, bead-pre-attempt-resolution, bead-attempt-resolution-e115609, bead-attempt-resolution-f25ab5c) sha256-MATCH their metadata files: the pin registry is internally consistent; only this one pair points at nothing.

(3) REPRODUCTION IS IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION even on a reachable tree: build.rs embeds wall-clock 'date -u' output and falls back to commit 'unknown' in a git-archive tree with no .git — two builds of one tree can never hash identically (already filed: beadrs-dc295092, beadrs-baba38b8). Toolchain is NOT drifted for the HEAD pin (rustc 1.97.1 installed = recorded 1.97.1); feature flags are a non-issue (Cargo.toml: attempt-resolution is an empty feature, default = []).

Shared checkout untouched throughout the run: only read-only git object queries; no build executed; stash list / reflog / HEAD / status unmodified.

Process note: this bead was closed twice by the dispatcher (actor system, reason 'verification is the gate's job (Phase 19.4)'; labeled over-budget). This note records the comparison result on the closed bead without reopening it. Follow-up: see the new bead filed against the unreachable pins (linked from the umbrella note).

ADDENDUM (2026-09-03, same session, minutes later): sibling workers landed scripts/build-from-archive.sh (uncommitted, beadrs-53e55a45 scope) and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH support in build.rs (uncommitted, beadrs-baba38b8 scope) in the shared checkout while this verification ran. The task's literal step was then executed with the real script: scripts/build-from-archive.sh <sha> invoked for all six recorded pins (af023ad, 946a727, 1ee45e3, e115609, f25ab5c, 6561869), --out redirected to a disposable scratch dir. RESULT: every run dies at SHA validation — "error: not a commit: <sha>", exit 1 — before creating any scratch dir or writing any file, so the earlier "script did not exist / no run possible" statement is superseded: the run HAS now been attempted with the sanctioned tool and fails on every recorded pin. Shared-checkout acceptance criterion verified by direct snapshot: git stash list, git reflog, HEAD (f4e4510) and the non-.beads git status are byte-identical before and after all six runs. Conclusion unchanged: NO MATCH, unobtainable as specified. Blocker (1) pin unreachability -> beadrs-e030cc56 (blocks beadrs-2257b877); blocker (3) determinism -> fix in flight (beadrs-dc295092 / beadrs-baba38b8).
issue.title: Verify the archive build reproduces the pinned binary sha256 recorded in COMMITS.md

issue.close_reason:
Circuit trigger was a checkpoint-churn race, not a source break - diff d7b8402..HEAD shows only .beads/checkpoint churn (six chore(beads) flush and unwedge revisions landing 12:30-12:33), zero delta on src, tests, Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock. Repair found nothing to fix, so no new revision was created and pre-existing dirty files (beads checkpoint churn plus another worker in-flight WIP in src/service/checkpoint.rs and src/store/migrations.rs) were left unstaged and untouched. Per HEAD-changed-circuit protocol the FULL DoD was run rather than --fast so clippy could not be masking a break: clean git-archive extraction of HEAD 07d6b4a at /var/tmp/beadrs-verify-923030-1790527098, scripts/definition-of-done.sh - cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test - all green, PASS, exit 0. Extraction removed after success. Checklist step 1 - status reviewed, no foreign files staged. Checklist step 4 - main pushed to Forgejo origin (d7b8402..07d6b4a fast-forward), rev-list origin/main..HEAD is empty, upstream current. Push initially failed because /home/coding/.git-credentials had flipped root-owned again (known recurring issue), restored ownership and retried successfully.
